passages.note: Aye on Assembly concurrence in Senate amendments, the final Assembly vote on the chaptered SAFETY Act text; 16 of 77 voting No, so not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent, unless otherwise required by state or federal law.
passages.note: Chaptered text (the text voted on in concurrence; Zbur also listed as principal coauthor); Section 220.5 forbids local rules requiring disclosure, and Section 220.3 only says staff are not required to disclose, so it does not require staff to withhold (rung 1) and requires no notice (rungs 3-5).

rows.reasoning: Zbur voted Aye on final Assembly passage (concurrence) of AB 1955 (2024), a single-subject pupil-rights bill whose operative Section 220.5 bars districts and charters from enacting or enforcing any policy that would require staff to disclose a pupil's gender identity without the pupil's consent. That matches the rung "Forbid rules that require schools to tell parents"; the bill does not require staff to keep the information from parents, so it does not reach the rung requiring secrecy unless the student consents.
